Verified twice post-creation with independent reads: get_report_v2(project_id=PR-2005, report_id=SC-489) returned 200 with the identical record, and list_reports_v2(project_id=PR-2005) returned total_report_count=1 (up from the sibling probe's established baseline of 0) with SC-489 as the sole row — so this is confirmed stored state, not an echo of the create response (the echo trap flagged for this batch does not apply cleanly here: the create response, the get_report_v2 read, and the list_reports_v2 row are all byte-for-byte identical, which is itself worth flagging to the sibling get_report_v2 probe as a data point, not proof of no drift on other capabilities).

MAIN FINDING (DRIFT): the capability's declared required set is wrong/misleading in two ways that point the same direction. First, describeCapability's machine-readable parameter list marks ONLY report_type, report_timeframe and report_creation_mode with required:true; title, frequency, mail_to and report_filters carry no required flag at all. Second, the capability's own prose guidance goes further and asserts outright that frequency, mail_to and report_filters 'are not' required despite the spec supposedly marking them so. Attempt 1 built the payload exactly per both of these signals (the 3 flagged-required fields plus title) and got a hard 400 naming report_filters, mail_to and frequency as missing required properties. So in truth the API requires those three keys to be PRESENT (trivial/empty values are accepted: 'once', {users:[],external_mails:[]}, {}) even though nothing in the contract said so and the guidance actively said the opposite. This is exactly the class of drift called out as the main event: a body shape built faithfully from the declared contract was rejected by the live API, and the fix (adding 3 undeclared-as-required keys) was needed to get a 201.

Secondary check: the 201 response body and the create-time 'returns' schema agree field-for-field — every key describeCapability's success schema promises (id, project_id, project_ids, report_type, title, description, report_timeframe, report_creation_mode, custom_date_range, frequency, frequency_details, next_run_at, is_scheduled, created_at, owner, mail_to, report_filters, dynamic_filters, latest_attachment) is present in the actual response, with matching shapes for nested objects (owner: email+full_name; mail_to: users+external_mails arrays; report_filters: the strict-allow-list object, empty here; dynamic_filters: null as documented). No undeclared extra fields were returned either. So the response-shape half of the contract is clean; the required-field half is the drift.
